chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, who said:

I heard al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying: A speaker said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'The man sits upon a rug in which are images.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The non-Arabs venerate it, and we belittle it.'

key_terms.الْأَعَاجِمُ: Non-Arabs (often referring to Persians or general non-Arab cultures in this context)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on sitting on rugs with images according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) articulates a pragmatic Shia jurisprudence regarding *tamyathil* (statues/depictions), distinguishing between the Persian cultural reverence for images and the Islamic principle of *istihlan* (devaluation). This hadith establishes that the presence of images on furnishings does not inherently render them impure or forbidden, provided they are not objects of worship, thereby allowing Muslims to utilize such items in daily life.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ismail Bin Mihran, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira who said,

‘I heard Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘A speaker said to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, ‘You<sup>asws</sup> make the man sit upon a rug in which are images’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The non-Arabs venerate it and we<sup>asws</sup> belittle it’.
en.sarwar: 7. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from ’Isma‘il ibn Mehran from ‘Abd Allah ibn al- Mughirah who has said the following:

“I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘Once a man asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al- Salam, if a man can sit on a furnishing which has pictures of things on it. He (the Imam) said, ‘Al-’A‘ajim (non- Arab) respect it, but we do not consider it important.’”
